comments.author: toomuchtodo
comments.story: Former Tesla Firmware Engineer Discusses the System
comments.why: Infotainment firewalled from CAN bus and critical systems
comments.text: Ignoring the infotainment system for this argument (as they firewall it off from CANBUS and other life critical systems [1]), I argue that their IT infrastructure is safety related, as it governs Tesla's velocity in getting patches and security fixes out to vehicles in a timely manner. Can you imagine a zero day being found in Windows with Windows Update being down? [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: toomuchtodo
comments.story: This Time, Miller and Valasek Hack the Jeep at Speed
comments.why: Tesla's gateway design for issuing CAN commands
comments.text: Indeed. Sending CAN frames directly is essentially a remote privilege escalation (think sudo user with no password). One of the shining examples of this done properly is Tesla; they have a gateway that you can issue commands to over the internal network, but it alone issues the CAN commands. You cannot issue CAN commands directly. [VIDEO]

comments.author: sweden
comments.why: DEF CON talk on rooting a Tesla Model S and remote shell access
comments.text: It is an interesting question. A while a go, 2 guys made a presentation at DEFCON with a presentation about their findings on hacking a Tesla Model S. They were able to successfully get root access to the car's system (not chroot, real full root access) and with that they were able to fully access to the car's API within Tesla OS. They even showed a video about one of the guys driving the car at low speed and the other one remotely accessing to the car's Linux shell by SSH and shutting down the whole car while the first guy was riding. The interesting thing is that for higher speeds, for example more than 50 km/h, the car seems to override any of the Linux systems and the root access becomes useless, it stops working. In another words, the car is able to decouple itself from the Tesla OS. You can check the presentation from those guys here: [VIDEO]
